title: C209 — Left-hand footwell lamp
introduction:
The left-hand footwell lamp's connection reads like a tiny lighting mixing desk: the Function column distinguishes the light-color feeds and the negative connection. I start with the connector identity, match a label in the drawing to the Cavity column, and then read that entire row. Keep wire Color separate from the color named in Function—one describes the wiring, the other the lighting role.

This page teaches the connector map and parts cross-reference. It does not provide physical access, a viewing-side designation, electrical test conditions or replacement instructions. The gauge convention and meanings of Box, Cols, Size and Used are undefined here. Retain the complete ambient-lighting configuration wording in each function without treating it as proof of the vehicle's equipment.

edits.why: The broad projection at the left and hooked outline at the lower right make the drawing asymmetrical. I use those landmarks to keep its displayed orientation clear while matching a printed cavity label to the table. They do not establish which side of a physical connector faces the viewer or show how to release it.

Follow the matching Cavity row through Circuit Number, Color, Gauge, the complete Function and Terminal Part Number. The function distinguishes a light-color feed from the negative connection; the wire-color code is a separate identifier. Keep the ambient-lighting configuration qualifier attached to the function. These associations identify the connection's listed role without proving that the lamp or controller operates correctly.

Use the kit, Service Part and Engineering Shell fields to understand the listed parts relationship. The pigtail's Gauge and Material describe that service entry; they do not replace the circuit-row specifications or authorize a splice method. I keep the Image filename as a reference to the named asset, without treating it as an installation illustration.
